ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in a classroom, a student stands on a weighing scale to study overweight and weightlessness. Her change from a stable standing posture to a stable squatting posture is called the “squatting down” process; her change from a stable squatting posture to a stable standing posture is called the “standing up” process. Regarding her experimental phenomena, which of the following statements is correct? ( )
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: In the processes of “standing up” and “squatting down,” phenomena of overweight and weightlessness can both occur.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a student can be seen standing on a weighing scale in a classroom environment. The problem discusses the phenomena of overweight and weightlessness corresponding to the reading of the weighing scale when she changes from a standing posture to a squatting posture and from a squatting posture to a standing posture on the weighing scale. Reasoning: The stem defines: changing from a stable standing posture to a stable squatting posture is called the “squatting down” process; changing from a stable squatting posture to a stable standing posture is called the “standing up” process. Because the initial and final states are both stable, each process includes two stages: starting to move from rest and finally decelerating to rest. To judge overweight or weightlessness, look at the direction of acceleration: when the acceleration is upward, the supporting force of the weighing scale is greater than gravity, and overweight occurs; when the acceleration is downward, the supporting force of the weighing scale is less than gravity, and weightlessness occurs. Squatting down process: at the beginning, she moves downward from rest and needs to accelerate downward, with acceleration downward, so weightlessness occurs; when approaching the stable squatting posture, the body is still moving downward but must decelerate and stop, with acceleration upward, so overweight occurs. Therefore, in the squatting down process, both weightlessness and overweight can occur. Standing up process: at the beginning, she moves upward from rest and needs to accelerate upward, with acceleration upward, so overweight occurs; when approaching the stable standing posture, the body is still moving upward but must decelerate and stop, with acceleration downward, so weightlessness occurs. Therefore, in the standing up process, both overweight and weightlessness can also occur. Final answer: both the standing up process and the squatting down process can have overweight and weightlessness phenomena.
